prompt:
Research the Kubernetes project's official policy on how many minor versions are supported at once and for how long each receives patches. Cite the Kubernetes documentation and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the official Kubernetes documentation, the project maintains support for the most recent three minor releases simultaneously. Regarding the duration of support, versions 1.19 and newer receive approximately one year of patch support, while versions 1.18 and older received approximately nine months.

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/ | QUOTE: "The Kubernetes project maintains release branches for the most recent three minor releases (1.37, 1.36, 1.35)." | CLAIM: The Kubernetes project officially supports the three most recent minor versions at any given time.

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/ | QUOTE: "Kubernetes 1.19 and newer receive approximately 1 year of patch support." | CLAIM: Minor versions released from 1.19 onwards are supported with patches for approximately one year.

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/ | QUOTE: "Kubernetes 1.18 and older received approximately 9 months of patch support." | CLAIM: Minor versions released prior to 1.19 were supported with patches for approximately nine months.

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/patch-releases/ | QUOTE: "In accordance with the yearly support KEP, the Kubernetes Community will support active patch release series for a period of roughly fourteen (14) months." | CLAIM: The total support period for an active patch release series is approximately 14 months, which includes a standard period and a maintenance mode period.

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/patch-releases/ | QUOTE: "The first twelve months of this timeframe will be considered the standard period." | CLAIM: The initial 12 months of the support window are designated as the standard support period.

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/patch-releases/ | QUOTE: "During the two-month maintenance mode period, Release Managers may cut additional maintenance releases to resolve: Vulnerabilities that have an assigned CVE ID... dependency issues... [and] critical core component issues" | CLAIM: The final two months of the support window are in maintenance mode, where only critical security and dependency fixes are released.
